title: Mix flour and liquid into a dough with a wooden spoon while steadying the loose mixing bowl by its grip tab
instruction: Mix the flour and the liquid in the bowl into a dough with the wooden spoon.
context: Mixing a dough or batter in a bowl with a spoon is one of the commonest steps in home cooking, and one of the hardest for people with weak grip or tremor, who use built-up spoon grips and bowls with handles like the ones here. Flour only takes up liquid where the spoon works it in, so the whole batch must be worked, not just the middle; a light steel bowl is pushed about by the spoon, so one hand steadies it by its tab while the other stirs. Unlike pouring, scooping or whisking tasks on the board, progress is the state of a few hundred particles, scored by how much dry flour is left.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Bowl: a loose 2.5 qt stainless mixing bowl (320 g), 21 cm across the rim, 13 cm across its flat base, 8.5 cm deep, base centred at x 33, y -4, on a laminate worktop (steel on laminate friction 0.25). On its left side (+y) a flat dark grip tab 4 cm out from the rim, 2.5 cm tall, 5 mm thick; on its near rim (toward the arms) a dark clip-on spoon rest: a shelf 2.2 cm out with two posts 14 mm apart and 2 cm tall. Spoon: a 26 cm beech spoon (head 6 x 4.5 cm, 1 cm thick; handle 12 x 9 mm, 52 g) with a blue built-up silicone grip, 50 mm long and 24 x 30 mm, its middle 19.9 cm from the tip. It stands in the clip leaning toward the arms 48 degrees from vertical, its tip on the bowl's floor 2.5 cm short of the middle, its grip about 15 cm above the table. Batch: 240 g of flour (160 white 12 mm beads) in a layer on the bowl's floor, with 140 g of egg and water (40 yellow beads) in a well in the middle. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, a kitchen scale and a sieve with 2 mm holes. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the bowl tips more than 30 degrees or more than 5% of the batch by weight (19 g) is out of the bowl. Otherwise score = the share of the flour mixed in, divided by 0.95, at most 1.0: 1.0 when 95% or more of the flour is mixed in, 0.5 at 47.5%, 0 when none is. Flour outside the bowl does not count. Real world: tip the bowl's contents onto the sieve and shake it 10 s; dry flour passes through. Mixed-in share = 1 - (mass through the sieve / 240 g). Simulator: a flour bead is mixed in (turns tan) once the spoon has worked it into the wet part: while the spoon's head moves through the batch faster than 3 cm/s, within 4 cm of its middle, touching liquid or mixed-in flour and sliding against it faster than 2 cm/s, for 1 cm in total. Read at the end of the run.
reset_notes: The batch is consumed: weigh out 240 g of flour, make a well, add 100 g of water and one egg (about 40 g). Wash and dry the bowl and spoon. Stand the spoon in its clip with its head in the flour.
fidelity: Flour and liquid are rigid 12 mm beads; dough's stickiness and stiffening are not modelled, and "mixed in" is a rule on the spoon working flour against liquid (sliding contact near the moving spoon's head), shown by the bead's colour. Bowl, tab, clip and spoon are rigid; the bowl's wall is 32 flat segments.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (knocked the spoon out of its clip; nothing mixed); demo: 1.0 (96% of the flour mixed in at step 1,218)
